name: Tabs
description: Tablist navigation with keyboard support and variant styles.

a11y.reviewedNote: 2026-05-26 — arrow-key navigation and selection verified in Storybook.

forbiddenUse: nest tablists inside another tablist. APG explicitly disallows
use Tabs for non-mutually-exclusive content. Two panels open
dense: Tablist-only tabs (parent renders panels via getTabPanelProps); variant default|pills|underline, size sm|md|lg; controlled activeTab/onTabChange or defaultActiveTab; roving arrow-key focus

usage.description: Tabs renders the tablist only — the parent owns the panels, pairing each to its tab with the exported `getTabPanelProps(key, isActive)` helper (or matching id/aria-labelledby/hidden attributes by hand). Drive it controlled with `activeTab` + `onTabChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultActiveTab`. Arrow keys move a roving focus through enabled tabs; `variant` picks the visual language (default, pills, underline) and `size` the density. Tabs switch views in place — they are not page navigation.

bestPractices.description: Render one tabpanel per tab and wire it with getTabPanelProps so aria-controls/aria-labelledby stay consistent.
Use controlled mode (activeTab + onTabChange) when the active tab should sync with URL or app state.
Keep tab labels to one or two words; tabs are a switch, not a table of contents.
Disable a tab with disabled on its item instead of removing it, so the set stays stable while unavailable.
Do not use tabs for page navigation — that is NavLink in a nav landmark; tabs switch views inside one page.
Do not lazy-delete panel DOM for inactive tabs that hold form state; hide them (hidden attr) so user input survives switching.
